name: Rajgira Paratha
steps: Boil the whole potatoes in a separate pan until a knife passes through the middle, about 20–25 minutes. Drain, cool enough to handle, peel and mash until smooth with no large lumps. The potatoes must not be watery.

Mix the rajgira flour, mashed potato, finely chopped green chilli, cumin, coriander and rock salt. Knead gently, adding the measured water a spoonful at a time only as needed, until the mixture holds together as a soft dough.

Divide the dough into eight balls. Flatten each between two sheets of baking parchment lightly greased with the measured ghee into a circle about 12 cm wide; rajgira contains no gluten, so pressing is safer than rolling hard. Peel away the upper sheet.

Heat a heavy griddle over medium heat. Invert one flatbread onto it, remove the remaining sheet and cook until the surface begins to dry. Turn carefully, brush with a little measured ghee and cook for 2–3 minutes until browned patches appear.

Brush the other side with ghee and cook until both faces are firm and the potato-amaranth centre is hot, not sticky. Repeat with the remaining dough and ghee. Serve two warm parathas per person; fasting rules vary by household, so check every ingredient against the household's own practice.
tips: Use genuine rajgira flour, not wheat flour. If the dough cracks, add a little of the measured water and press between parchment instead of stretching it.
passiveTime: Allow the boiled potato to cool before making the dough.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
